current.text: He is in Cleveland's projected starting lineup at center, next to James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Peyton Watson and Evan Mobley.
His minutes sometimes drop and he sits out some fourth quarters.
His minutes are at risk if Cleveland plays Mobley more at center or closes games with Mobley at center after adding Peyton Watson. One expert does not see him reaching 30 minutes a game.
Cleveland's big-man depth is very thin. Only Thomas Bryant is behind Mobley and Allen, then Ernest Udeh Jr. and Khalifa Diop. Dean Wade is gone, which removes the small-ball center option.
The weak backup center group and Wade's departure help protect his role.

With Harden on the floor last season he averaged 25 points and 13 rebounds per 36 minutes on 71% shooting with 23% usage. Without Harden it was 19 points and 11 rebounds per 36 minutes on 62% shooting. He played well in February with Harden and with Mobley out.
A full season of Harden could lift his efficiency. At 66 to 67% from the field on 21 to 22% usage he could score about 17 points and be a top 70 player.
He had a knee injury late last season. Cleveland reports no current injury concerns.
He finished around 69th to 79th last season, depending on format, and 79th per game.
Experts value him around picks 70 to 86, about round 7. He is a solid but boring pick with little upside and some downside.
His ESPN rank around 49 to 53 is far too high. Experts call him a strong no and a top fade at that price.
Take him mainly when you need a center. Otherwise one expert prefers players like Paul George at the same spot.
Cleveland has one of the most back-to-back heavy schedules in the league.
With a March 28 end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and then 2 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is 9 games, with a two-game finals week.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games. Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.

durable.text: He is a rebounding and field goal percentage center. His FG% on solid volume is a league-level strength.
He no longer blocks many shots for a center.
His usual FG% is around 64%. His true level is probably between his 63.8% and 70.6% seasons.
His free throws are rough, but not as bad as Rudy Gobert's.
He is a prime example of nine-cat fluff. Z-score rankings that include turnovers make him look better than he really is.

note: Experts put Allen around picks 70 to 86. Yahoo values him at 12 USD, ESPN at 10 USD, and our league paid 13 USD last season. Yahoo drafters pay only 3.1 USD on average, so 8 to 12 USD is fair, but do not pay for his ESPN rank of 51. He fits punt 3PM builds and teams that want FG% and rebounds from a center. Early in the season, check his minutes, whether Mobley closes games at center, and whether his FG% sits nearer 64% or 70% next to Harden.
